title: rules.huginn.php.tainted-command-execution
message: Untrusted PHP request input reaches operating-system command execution.
reviewer_decision: known vulnerability: CVE-2026-101859 still present in 3.5.7
reviewer_notes: Known issue CVE-2026-101859 (cfg_id argument injection past escapeshellcmd in ajax/openvpn/del_ovpncfg.php; follows CVE-2022-39986). The CVE lists "up to 3.5.5", but del_ovpncfg.php is byte-identical in 3.5.5, 3.5.6 and 3.5.7 (tag 3.5.7 = 8a20150), and the sudoers rule "/bin/rm /etc/openvpn/client/*.conf" still lets the wildcard span injected arguments. So the published affected range looks incomplete: 3.5.7 is still affected. Requires an authenticated session plus CSRF token (RASPI_AUTH_ENABLED defaults to true). Not a new finding; the maintainer contact is security@raspap.com if the range needs correcting.

title: rules.huginn.javascript.tainted-ssrf
message: Untrusted JavaScript/TypeScript input reaches an outbound request target.
reviewer_decision: true positive: unauthenticated toolbox proxy sends stored Jira credentials to a caller-chosen host (CWE-522, CWE-918)
reviewer_notes: agento/modules/jira/toolbox/jira-proxy.js: host = req.body.jira_host || config.host while user/token fall back to the configured global Jira credentials (getJiraConfig(null)); fetch(`${host}${path}`) sends Authorization: Basic user:token to that host and returns the body. POST /api/jira/request is registered on the toolbox Express app, which authenticates no caller (server.js: "the internal Docker network IS its boundary") and listens on 0.0.0.0:3001; the agent sandbox container shares agento-net (docker-compose template), so a prompt-injected agent can exfiltrate the tool credential the README says the sandbox never holds. Affected 0.6.0 through 0.16.3 (latest stable, 2026-09-29). Fixed in pre-release 0.17.0rc2 (host no longer overridable, path must be host-relative). Pipeline OSV/GHSA/NVD lookup NO_MATCH; sdist sha256 recorded in artifact_sha256.

reviewer_decision: true positive: missing authentication on network tool server (CWE-306) reaching shell=True exec
reviewer_notes: tool_server.py create_app() is served by main.py on host 0.0.0.0 port 8990 with no authentication on any route; _is_loopback_request() exists but is applied only to /analysis/full. POST /tools/exec_command passes body["cmd"] to subprocess.run(shell=True) when control.enabled and control.allow_exec are set (opt-in, documented as DANGEROUS), giving unauthenticated RCE to anyone who can reach the port. README documents the port as the network callback URL for Archilence Core, so network exposure is the intended deployment. Only the opt-in PIPULATE_TOOL_DENY env var removes it. So anyone who can reach port 5001 (same LAN, or a cross-site request if the browser allows it, since request.json() does not check Content-Type) runs shell commands as the user. The flagged /open-folder route (subprocess open/xdg-open/explorer on any existing directory) is the same unauthenticated surface; on macOS it also launches any .app bundle. Affected: 1.2.0 (2025-09-25, first release with execute_shell_command in the registry) through 2.72 (2026-09-30); checked 1.2.0, 1.2.3, 1.5, 1.96, 2.0, 2.3, 2.41, 2.50, 2.60, 2.71, 2.72. 1.1.1 already binds 0.0.0.0 with the executor but has no shell tool. 2.72 sdist sha256 recorded in docs/disclosures/pipulate.md.
